excluded.question: M075-Q01

excluded.question: M079-Q01
excluded.detail: The Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 and the Age of Majority Ordinance are absent from the frozen corpus, and the effect of a minor's deed of transfer and of a Thesawalamai disposition made without the husband's written consent turns on Roman-Dutch common law and judicial authority. The devolution of Lot 5A therefore cannot be settled on statute alone; the Lot 5B branch of the pedigree is complete and is set out in question M079-Q02. Verifier: the block stands and is wider than stated. Civil Procedure Code s.582 only bars an uncertificated person from instituting or defending an action connected with a minor's estate, so nothing in the corpus makes Deed of Transfer No. 1234 defective as to Lot 5A; and Jaffna Ordinance s.6 governs the wife's separate estate, so its written-consent rule does not plainly reach lots the same map treats as thediatheddam bought for value under s.19(a). Claims CL-M079-Q01-003 and CL-M079-Q01-007 are rejected on that footing.

excluded.question: M079-Q03
excluded.detail: The Age of Majority Ordinance, which fixes the general age of majority, is not in the frozen corpus; Civil Procedure Code s.502 fixes full age at eighteen only for the purposes of its own chapter. The requirement that a curator obtain the District Court's sanction before alienating a minor's immovable property, and the effect of failing to do so, come from Roman-Dutch common law and judicial authority rather than from any section in this corpus. The second and third instances are fully supported by statute; the first is not. Verifier: the second and third instances are weaker than the map states. Civil Procedure Code s.582 says a claimant may apply for a certificate of curatorship and makes the certificate mandatory only for instituting or defending an action, so no section in this corpus requires a curator to be joined as executant of Deed of Transfer No. 1234; and Jaffna Ordinance s.6 reaches the wife's separate estate, while s.8 supplies a District Court order only in the enumerated cases, none of which is present. Claims CL-M079-Q03-001 and CL-M079-Q03-005 are rejected and the Executor's Conveyance instance under s.530 is the only one that stands on statute alone.

excluded.question: M081-Q02

No Western Province stamp duty rate Order or rate schedule in force in October 2019 exists in the frozen corpus, and searches for rate language across the corpus return nothing. The chargeable value of Rs.3,020,000 and the liability of the grantee are supportable from the corpus, but the money amount of duty the question asks for cannot be computed without inventing or recalling a rate, which this task forbids.

excluded.question: M086-Q01
excluded.detail: The question asks which type of deed to draw, and no provision in the frozen corpus names a deed of declaration or prescribes its form. The corpus reaches the instrument only obliquely, through section 8(b) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, which deems an instrument that declares a right, title or interest in land to be registrable. A second indispensable step is also outside the corpus: section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance is expressed as a rule of proof entitling a party to a decree in an action, and nothing in the corpus states that prescriptive title vests without a decree so that the possessor may declare it by deed. Both steps rest on conveyancing practice and judicial authority, so the question is mixed_statute_and_case and cannot be proposed_gold. The statutory scaffolding recorded above is complete and can be verified as it stands.

Verifier: the s.8 consent point is unresolved rather than merely unlikely, because the corpus holds no repealing or amending instrument for s.8 and the related s.11 dispensation procedure was not recorded; the question stays reserved.

excluded.question: M089-Q01
excluded.detail: The controlling law is the Roman-Dutch common law of praedial servitudes (appurtenance to the dominant tenement, effect of subdivision of the dominant tenement, aggravation of the servient burden), which is not in the frozen corpus. excluded.question: M089-Q02

Verifier: agreed, and PROV-M089-003 is demoted from supporting to background because an interpretation clause of the Municipal Councils Ordinance cannot state the general rule. The corpus does hold one statutory route to a right of way that the map does not mention - Prescription Ordinance s.3 read with the s.2 definition of immovable property, which includes servitudes appertaining to it - but on these facts Kapila Fernando has no user of Lot R1 at all, so it does not answer the question.

excluded.question: M094-Q02
excluded.detail: The authority requirement is statute_only, but the corpus carries only the consolidated post-2022 and post-2024 text of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance. Two of the rules that decide this question changed after the April 2019 matter date: rule (9) was substituted in 2022 and again in 2024, and rule (20)(b), the paragraph that carries the 'not known to me but known to the witnesses' recital, was substituted in 2022 with wording that adds identification by national identity card, passport or driving licence. Rule (20)(h), requiring the attestation of a will to state that the testator was of sound mind, was only inserted in 2022. Form E of the Second Schedule, prescribed by rule (21), is absent from the corpus, and the only Form E text available is the 2022 replacement. The April 2019 wording of rule (9) survives verbatim only in the recital in section 16(6) of Act No. 31 of 2022. The draft attestation is therefore proposed subject to confirmation against the 2019 edition of the Ordinance and Form E as it then stood.
